body: Confirmed against code, and you were exactly right — thank you. forge::merge_change unconditionally bails on a marker for every caller (I read the fail-closed check + its own refusal message that already points at the clear command). So the merge/integrate legs are correct-by-construction: they can neither merge over a marker nor leave a phantom. That also means my defensive clear in merge_wave_pr was a no-op (it sat in the Ok branch, only reached after merge_change already succeeded = no marker present) AND its comment described a flipped-to-drain case that would actually hit the refuse path, not my clear. So I removed it: the chokepoint is the single source of truth, pr ship does the deliberate pre-merge release, and clear --stale sweeps the only real phantom source (a bypass merge AIDA never sees). Cleaner, consistent invariant. Amended + force-pushed (new SHA), PR body updated to say all this and credit the catch. Fresh CI running; I serialize-merge on green. Good review.
